Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with a wrist fracture, and the reported injury is consistent
with the mechanism and force of the crash. Initial imaging confirmed the fracture, and the patient was immobilized
and then transitioned to a structured rehabilitation plan. Over the course of thirteen visits, treatment extended
somewhat beyond the typical timeframe for this injury, reflecting a slower-than-expected return to function.
Examination findings include localized tenderness and reduced grip strength on the affected side that support the
diagnosis, while several other tests, including neurovascular assessment and sensation, returned normal. No prior
injury to the same area is known from the patient history. Billing records reflect single, non-duplicated charges for
each service rendered. Ongoing monitoring continues, with restrictions on heavy lifting maintained until radiographic
and functional healing is confirmed.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
